Thanks Rafael — reviewing.

Quick answers and next steps:
- We can produce a single consolidated invoice that contains line-level remittance instructions (common approach). Our AR system will export one invoice PDF but each line can include a "Remit to" note and bank details. This keeps one accounting document while enabling collections to apply payments to separate GL buckets.
- VAT treatment: for EU entity purchases we will issue a VAT-inclusive invoice to the EU legal entity. If Nimbus provides a valid VAT ID and is the buyer in the EU, reverse-charge could apply — we'll flag Finance to confirm. Ben, please confirm treatment and whether Redwood needs to report VAT on the EU sale.
- Escrow handling: we typically do not act as escrow agent. For the 20% holdback we can: (A) create the invoice with the 20% line marked "Payable to Nimbus Escrow" with their escrow account details provided (preferred by customer), OR (B) Redwood can issue the invoice and receive funds into our escrow sub-account and disburse later — this requires legal sign-off. Option A reduces our liability.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm VAT reporting / reverse-charge by EOD 2026-08-12.
- Marissa: confirm whether Finance can accept a single-PDF invoice with line-level remits and how payments will map to GL.
- Rafael: once we confirm Bank details from Nimbus, I will build the invoice and push DocuSign envelope for the amended SOW/invoice.

Attaching: split-invoice-proposal.pdf (mockup)
